briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Brands Go National as DC Clears the Path for Cannabis
briefs.top: Michigan operators are turning tax pain into political leverage and market share — a homegrown chain is buying its way into Arizona while the GOP governor nominee campaigns on killing the 24% wholesale tax. Nationally, courts and regulators keep nudging cannabis toward the mainstream even as a blockbuster hostile takeover fight and a slow-moving DEA process remind everyone the shift isn't finished yet.

local.text: Michigan's JARS Cannabis expands into Arizona — JARS Cannabis announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa brand dispensaries, a move that will soon make JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.
Muskegon's Fields Cannary targets fall opening — Fields Cannary, a Muskegon development, is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow.

Grön's Pearls gummies land on Michigan shelves — Grön, a Portland edibles brand owned by Wyld, put its bestselling 'Pearls' gummies into Michigan dispensaries as part of a four-state rollout, already confirmed at Pure Options, High Profile, and Lume.

Small towns keep cashing in on Michigan weed — New Buffalo Township, with a population of roughly 2,500, hosts 26 marijuana businesses and collects $1.4 million in annual cannabis tax revenue, a standout example of how opt-in towns benefit from neighbors' opt-out decisions.

GOP nominee pledges to repeal the 24% tax — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association has officially endorsed Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, citing his commitment to repealing the 24% wholesale tax, and Michigan's cannabis industry executives wrote him about $90,000 in checks this summer backing his candidacy for governor.

national.text: Federal court upholds medical marijuana rescheduling — Reclassification opponents filed a lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's change in schedule, but that challenge was rebuffed this week in federal court, with the D.C. Circuit leaving the rescheduling order in effect.

DEA's own lawyers argue weed doesn't fit Schedule I — in its own final post-hearing brief the DEA argued that marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, though the administrative law judge has not yet issued a recommendation.

FDA fast-tracks Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy — on April 24, 2026, the FDA issued Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers to three psychedelic programs, including Compass Pathways' COMP360 psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression, a tool that shortens standard review to roughly one to two months.

Trulieve becomes first plant-touching MSO on NYSE — Trulieve Cannabis Corp. received approval to list on the New York Stock Exchange beginning June 10 under ticker TRLV, marking a historic shift for U.S. plant-touching operators after executing a restructuring to maintain a 100% medical footprint following federal Schedule III reclassification.

Curaleaf-Aurora hostile takeover battle escalates — Curaleaf published a second public rebuttal to Aurora's directors' circular, part of a bid worth about $272 million that has been open since Aug. 18 and expires Dec. 1, with Curaleaf urging Aurora shareholders on Sept. 15 to accept the offer, realize a 45% premium, and join the world's leading cannabis company.
